title: Audit record added with a library that was not supplied: its flush behavior is an unresolved fact, not a High

proof.shell:
W=$PWD; T=$(mktemp -d); cp -r base/. $T/ && cd $T && patch -p1 -s < $W/change.patch && python3 - <<'PYEND'
import subprocess, sys
r = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-m", "unittest", "-q", "tests.test_orders"], capture_output=True, text=True, env={"PYTHONPATH": ".", "PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE": "1"})
assert r.returncode == 0, r.stderr
r = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-c", "import orders"], capture_output=True, text=True, env={"PYTHONPATH": ".", "PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE": "1"})
assert r.returncode != 0 and "company_audit" in r.stderr, "the library must be genuinely absent"

PYEND

suspicions.why: whether record() is written before it returns or queued and lost when the process exits is not knowable from what was supplied
